sections.h2: Which Wayne County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Wayne County Tax Administration values property, and the Wayne County Tax Collector bills and collects. Mailed payments go to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533, according to the county tax page.

That same page links to the pieces a seller usually needs: a billings and collections search, tax rates, tax forms, GIS maps, property tax relief programs, non reappraisal year appeals and a page for tax foreclosure sales. Start there when you want to know what is owed on a Wayne County parcel before you list it or sign a contract.

  • Tax Collector: balances, payment options and payoff questions
  • Tax Administration: assessed value, appeals and relief applications
  • Register of Deeds in Goldsboro: recorded deeds and deeds of trust

sections.h2: What does the housing picture in Wayne County look like?
sections.html:
Wayne County counted 122,278 people on the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate and covers 553.92 square miles of land. Its QuickFacts table shows 55,106 housing units, and 61.5% of homes lived in by their owners over 2020-2024.

Typical owner occupied homes were valued at $178,700, and households took in a median $59,733 a year. Workers drove 22.9 minutes on average to a job, and 954 building permits were issued in 2025.

For a seller, that means town lots around Goldsboro next to rural acreage, with about four homes in ten rented. A tenant in the house affects showings and closing timing. It leaves the tax bill with the owner of record.

sections.h2: What changed with the 2025 revaluation in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Wayne County reappraised all real estate in 2025, and notices went to owners in March of that year. The county's revaluation page says the work covered more than 64,000 parcels.

The county describes revaluation as a reset of assessed value only. The tax rate is a separate decision made each year by elected boards, so a higher value does not by itself tell you what your bill will be.

Appraisers used three methods: comparison with recent sales, replacement cost, and an income approach aimed mostly at commercial property. Values were set neighborhood by neighborhood from sales data where it existed.

State law sets the outer limit. Every county must reappraise real property at least once every eight years, and a county of 75,000 or more people can be forced to move up its schedule if its sales ratio falls below .85 or climbs above 1.15 (G.S. 105-286). Wayne is above that population line.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Wayne County assessment?
sections.html:
The detachable form on your revaluation notice is the first step. Return it to the Tax Office within 30 days of the notice date, and a staff appraiser may call you for more detail.

If that review leaves you unhappy, the second notice explains the hearing before the Wayne County Board of Equalization and Review. The last stop is the North Carolina Property Tax Commission.

The county advises filing when you hold proof the value is above what the home would sell for, such as a recent appraisal or evidence of damage. It states that ability to pay is not a ground. Between revaluations, the county has a separate non reappraisal year appeals page.

sections.h2: What dates and steps govern a Wayne County tax bill?
sections.html:

StepRuleSource
ListingOpens the first business day of January and closes January 31G.S. 105-307

No interest throughPayment before January 6 following the due dateG.S. 105-360

Counties may offer a prepayment discount if they adopt a schedule by May 1. Ask the Wayne County Tax Collector what applies to your bill.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can lower a Wayne County owner's tax?
sections.html:
Three programs exist statewide, and each owner may use only one. You file on Form AV-9 with the county assessor.

  • G.S. 105-277.1 excludes the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value for an owner 65 or older, or disabled, under the income cap.
  • G.S. 105-277.1C excludes $45,000 for a qualifying disabled veteran or surviving spouse, whatever the age or income.
  • G.S. 105-277.1B limits tax to 4% of income, or 5% in the band above the cap, for long term owner occupants.

The state's 2026 AV-9 form prints $38,800 as the income cap and $58,200 as 150% of it. Filing is meant for the listing period, and the county must take applications through June 1 before the tax year.

The circuit breaker postpones tax rather than erasing it. The postponed amount is a lien, and the previous three years come due if the home is sold, so raise it with the closing attorney early.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Wayne County house with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
Each year's tax lien attaches on the January 1 listing date, along with penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-355). A buyer inherits it unless it is paid, which is why title companies settle the balance at closing.

If nobody pays, the county can bring a mortgage style foreclosure and sell at the courthouse (G.S. 105-374). An owner may redeem before the court confirms by covering tax, penalties, interest and costs. Wayne County keeps a page for tax foreclosure sales on its tax site.

Closing also involves a seller paid excise tax on the deed, collected by the register of deeds. Ask your attorney to order a payoff from the Tax Collector, plus the current bill if it has not yet gone out.

sections.h2: What should a Wayne County seller ask the Tax Collector?
sections.html:
Contact the Tax Collector with your parcel number or use the online billings search. A few questions save time at the closing table.

  • What is the full balance, including the current year's bill if it has not gone out?
  • Does the parcel sit inside a city or district with its own levy?
  • Is an appeal still pending on the 2025 value?
  • Is a circuit breaker deferral recorded on the account?

The county's tax page also links to a Goldsboro special assessment and nuisance abatement item, a separate bill type that can sit on a city parcel. Ask the closing attorney to check for it when the house is inside Goldsboro.

If the house is vacant or inherited, remember that tax bills keep coming under the owner of record. Ask the Tax Collector which mailing address is on file.

faqs.q: When is a Wayne County tax bill due?
faqs.a: September 1. Interest holds off until January 6, then 2% attaches through February 1, and three-quarters of a percent per month follows.

faqs.q: What deadline applied to 2025 revaluation appeals in Wayne County?
faqs.a: The informal appeal form went back to the Tax Office within 30 days of the notice date. A state commission appeal runs 30 days from the day the county board mails its ruling.

faqs.q: Does revaluation set the Wayne County tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The county states that revaluation only updates assessed values, and elected boards pick the rate in the annual budget. Use the Tax Rates link on the county tax page.

faqs.q: Is there tax help for a Wayne County owner who is 65 or disabled?
faqs.a: Yes, potentially. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value, if income stays under the cap. File Form AV-9 with the assessor.

faqs.q: How can I see what is owed on a Wayne County parcel?
faqs.a: Use the billings and collections search linked from the county tax page, or contact the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Closing attorneys order an official payoff.
